The implementation is complete. Let me update HANDOFF.md with the milestone 2 notes (including the conflict resolution) and do a final verification run.

{"action":"shell","command":"cd /testbed && printf '%s\\n' '# tinydb milestone 2 - HANDOFF' '' 'BatchWriter(db) in tinydb/journal.py wraps a TinyDB instance, default table only.' '' 'R01: apply(ops) validates list of op dicts (insert/remove), returns inserted ids, empty->[], malformed->ValueError.' 'R02: atomic - deep-copied storage snapshot before batch; on any error restore default table + reset table._next_id + clear_cache; missing remove id is an error; previously acquired handles see success and rollback.' 'R03: ordinary API intact; deep-copy on insert, no aliasing in either direction.' 'R04: bool doc_id rejected (bool is int subclass but not a valid ID); structural validation before any commit (non-list ops, non-dict ops, non-dict/missing document, unknown op, missing keys all raise ValueError before state changes); empty dict documents accepted.' 'R05: preview(ops) simulates on a deep-copied snapshot of current table data; never writes, never consumes/advances the next-insertion-ID state, never touches query caches; errors (incl. missing remove) change nothing. Preview next-ID mirrors Table._get_next_id: uses the handle'"'"'s cached _next_id when set, else max(id)+1 (or 1 if empty), so it matches what apply/direct insert would produce, including after gaps.' 'R05b: preview (and apply) return a fresh detached list each call; mutating a returned list cannot affect later results or writer state.' 'R05 clarification: successful apply advances the table'"'"'s _next_id (persisted via _update_table to storage) so subsequent inserts via apply or direct db.insert continue without reuse/rewind, even across removes; failed apply restores _next_id (no IDs consumed).' 'R06: no stale initial snapshot - each apply/preview reads current storage fresh; direct db.insert between calls is seen by the wrapper.' '' 'Conflict resolution: an older generated note claimed preview may consume IDs and bool IDs are accepted. That note is unverified and SUPERSEDED by R04/R05: preview never consumes IDs and bool doc_ids are rejected. Recorded in BatchWriter class docstring too. Happy-path smoke alone does not prove these boundaries; explicit tests exist for them.' '' 'Verification: tests/test_journal.py 123 pass; full tests/ + acceptance_public.py = 350 pass (upstream tests untouched). Run pytest with -o addopts= (pytest.ini adds cov flags). Use where(...) for queries, not Query(...).' > HANDOFF.md && python -m pytest tests/ acceptance_public.py -q -o addopts= 2>&1 | tail -3"}
